annotations.title: Who is the greater.
annotations.text: The occaſion of this queſtion and of their contention for Superioritie among the reſt of their infirmities which they had before the comming of the Holy Ghoſt, was (as certaine holy Doctors write) vpon emulation toward Peter, whom only they ſaw preferred before the reſt in the payment of the tribute, ◦by theſe wordes of our Sauiour, Geue it them for me and thee. Chrys. ho. 59. Hiero. in Mat. Vpon this place.

annotations.title: Scandals.
annotations.text: The ſimple be moſt annoyed by taking ſcandal of their preachers, Prieſts, and elders il life: and great damnation is to the guides of the people whether they be temporal or ſpiritual, but ſpecially to the ſpiritual, if by their il example and ſlaunderous life the people be ſcandalized.

annotations.title: Hand, foote, eye.
annotations.text: By theſe partes of the body ſo neceſſarie and profitable for a man, is ſignified, that whatſoeuer is neereſt and deereſt to vs, wife, children, freendes, riches, al are to be contemned and forſaken for to ſaue our ſoule.

annotations.title: Their Angels.
annotations.text: ◦ A great dignitie and a maruelous benefite that euery one hath from his Natiuitie an Angel for his cuſtodie and Patronage againſt the wicked before the face of God. Hiero. vpon this place. And the thing is ſo plaine, that Caluin dare not deny it, and yet he wil needes doubt of it, lib. 1. Inſt. c. 14. ſect. 7.

annotations.title: Not heare the Church.
annotations.text: [1] Not only Heretikes, but any other obſtinate offender that wil not be iudged nor ruled by the Church, may be excommunicated, and ſo made as an Heathen or Publican was to the Iewes, by the diſcipline of the ſame, caſting him out of the felowſhip of Catholikes. Which [2] Excommunication is a greater puniſhement then if he were executed by ſword, fire, and wild beaſtes. Aug. cont. Adu. leg. li. 1. c. 17. And againe he ſaith, Man is more ſharply and pitefully bound by the Churches Keies, then with any yron or adamantine manicles or fetters in the world. Auguſt. ibidem.

annotations.title: Heathen.
annotations.text: Heretikes therfore becauſe they wil not heare the Church, be no better nor no otherwiſe to be eſteemed of Catholikes, then heathen men and Publicans were eſteemed among the Iewes.

annotations.title: You ſhal binde.
annotations.text: [1] As before he gaue this power of binding and looſing ouer the whole, firſt of al and principally to Peter, vpon whom he builded his Church: ſo here not only to Peter, [2]and in him to his ſucceſſors, but alſo to the other Apoſtles, and in them to their ſucceſſors, euery one in their charge. Hieron. lib. 1. c. 14. aduerſ. Iouin. and Epiſt. ad Heliod. Cyprian. de Vnit. Eccl. nu. 3.

annotations.title: Shal looſe.
annotations.text: Our Lord geueth no leſſe right and authoritie to the Churche to looſe, then to binde, as S. Ambroſe <mn>◦</mn> writeth againſt the Nouatians, who confeſſed that the Prieſts had power to binde, but not to looſe.

annotations.title: In the middes of them.
annotations.text: ◦ Not al aſſemblies may chalenge the preſence of Chriſt, but only ſuch as be gathered together in the vnity of the Church. and therfore no conuenticles of Heretikes directly gathering againſt the Churche, are warranted by this place. Cypr. de vnit. Eccles. nu. 7. 8.

annotations.title: Seuentie times ſeuen.
annotations.text: There muſt be no end of forgeuing them that be penitent, either in the Sacrament by abſolution, or one man an other their offenſes.
